digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler — inbound link removal and graph layer link store
propositions: Inbound link removal declines permanently at guard G5 when a pair holds two net-active relations (blocks and relates_to) and the outbound differ emits no link mutation for the pair, causing non-convergence on every reconcile pass.

Write operations use (target_id, relation) as the idempotency key allowing one pair to hold multiple relations, but removal is pair-scoped (no relation argument) and queries only the most-recent net-active link, causing the asymmetry.

A double-related pair whose peer drops one relation never converges because the inbound removal record names a relation that does not match the pair's most-recent net-active link, triggering permanent decline without operator-visible signal beyond log lines.

The fix makes removal symmetric with writes by adding a relation-scoped seam graph/_links.py::remove_dependency that validates and removes the exact (target_id, relation) link, mirroring add_dependency behavior.

The reconciler's _inbound_unlink_one must switch from pair-scoped to relation-scoped removal so that G5's decline case converges by removing exactly the mirrored relation instead of permanently declining.
CLI rebar unlink gains an optional relation argument for backward-compatible relation-scoped removal; with no relation the existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is unchanged.
